findings.element: Actions cell of Done rows in the 'Line Analysis DPM' and 'Trip Failures DPM' accordions
findings.finding: Finished evaluations in two of the six type groups expose only a Delete icon, so no control anywhere on the screen opens their report.
findings.user_impact: A user who locates the completed Line Analysis or Trip Failures evaluation they came for cannot read its result and the primary task dead-ends on a row that says Done.
findings.suggested_fix: Give every row whose status is Done an opener, or render a disabled opener with an inline reason stating why that result cannot be viewed.

evidence.action: In the 'Line Analysis DPM' group, went to the Actions cell of a row whose Status reads Done and looked for the preview (eye) control used on Done Punctuality rows; repeated in 'Trip Failures DPM'.
evidence.observed: Both cells contain a single Delete icon and nothing else — recorded action sets are done:line_analysis = delete and done:trip_failures = delete, versus visibility+delete on done:punctuality, done:data_quality and done:connection.

findings.element: Download icon on Done rows in the 'Raw Data Export DPM' accordion
findings.finding: The download action reports success in a snackbar reading 'Download started …' but no file is ever produced and no terminal state follows.
findings.user_impact: The user believes the export is on its way, waits for a file that never arrives, and either re-clicks the icon repeatedly or abandons the evaluation without its content.
findings.suggested_fix: Deliver the file, or replace the premature success message with an in-progress state that resolves to an explicit ready-or-failed outcome with a retry.

evidence.action: Clicked the download icon on a Done row in the 'Raw Data Export DPM' group.
evidence.observed: A snackbar reading 'Download started …' appeared; no file was produced and the row never reached any further state.

findings.element: Evaluation name cell and the Actions column, all six tables
findings.finding: The obvious target — the evaluation name — is inert text, while the only opener is a small unlabeled icon whose presence and meaning change from row to row with nothing on screen explaining the rule.
findings.user_impact: Users click the name first and get nothing, then have to probe icons row by row across 28 rows to discover which evaluations can be opened, turning a lookup into trial and error.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the evaluation name the primary link to the report wherever one exists, and keep the row's action set stable by showing disabled-with-reason controls instead of omitting them.

evidence.action: Clicked the evaluation name in a 'Punctuality DPM' row, then compared the Actions cells of a Done Punctuality row, a Done Raw Data Export row and an In Progress row.
evidence.observed: The name is plain text with no link affordance and the click did nothing; the three rows rendered visibility+delete, download+delete and delete respectively — three different action sets, none labelled.

findings.element: Top bar links Startseite / Q.Reports / Fotoalbum / Q-Messungen, and login links Impressum / Dokumente / Kontaktdaten / Support plus 'Forgot your password?'
findings.finding: Nine links render as live navigation — the four login utility links even carry an open-in-new icon — yet every one is a dead click with no destination and no message.
findings.user_impact: Users spend clicks on targets that never respond and get no signal about whether the app is broken or the feature simply is not here, the exact dead-click pattern recorded in KF-4.
findings.suggested_fix: Either wire these to a destination or render them visibly non-interactive, and have any that must remain say 'not part of this prototype' on click.

evidence.action: Clicked 'Q.Reports' in the top bar, then 'Impressum' on the login screen, then 'Forgot your password?'.
evidence.observed: Nothing happened on any of the three — no navigation, no dialog, no message; the top-bar items are only dimmed to 75% opacity and the login links keep their open-in-new icon.

findings.element: Six type accordions with repeated table headers, and the non-sortable column headers
findings.finding: The 28 evaluations are split across six separately headed tables and no column anywhere can be sorted, so there is no single ordered view of the list.
findings.user_impact: A user who knows what they want only approximately — the newest run, the one from last month, the failed one — must scan six tables by eye, because the list can never be ordered by Created, Status or Period.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the Created, Status and Period headers sortable, or offer a flat all-evaluations view that can be ordered independently of the type grouping.

evidence.action: Clicked the 'Created' column header in the 'Punctuality DPM' table, then scrolled the full list top to bottom.
evidence.observed: The header did not sort and carries no sort affordance; the same Name|Period|Created|Status|Actions header repeats once per group, six times over the 28 rows.

gaps: Live verification could not be performed: the browser tool returned a closed-scope error on every call, so nothing beyond the state map could be confirmed first-hand and every finding above rests on recorded state-map behaviour.
Preview (eye) is recorded as 'opens the report', but report views beyond the first screen are in not_exercised — so whether the primary task actually completes after that click is unverified.
Run on the New evaluation page is in not_exercised, so the second branch of the primary task ('or start a new one') has no recorded completion and its success/error state is unknown.

No interaction between filters and collapsed accordions was recorded — whether a Status or Period match inside a collapsed group is revealed or stays hidden is unknown, and that determines whether filtering can silently hide results.
The count subtitle is recorded as following the filters but not as following accordion collapse, so it is unknown whether it still reads '28 evaluations' while only 22 rows are visible.
The 'No evaluations found' empty state is recorded only for Search; the map does not record what it offers as a way out, nor what a zero-result Status+Period combination displays.
No loading or in-flight state is recorded for any control — filters, accordions, report open or download — so whether long operations communicate progress (KF-1) could not be assessed.
The Period option 'Other' was never picked, so whether it opens a custom range, and how that range commits, is unrecorded.
In-progress rows are recorded as existing but no progress indicator, elapsed time or terminal transition was recorded for them, so what a user sees while waiting for a run is unknown.
